activeExercises.title: Greetings & Introductions
activeExercises.instr: Listen to the greeting and choose the best response to introduce yourself in English.
activeExercises.audioText: Hello! Welcome to our school. What is your name?

dialogue.speaker: Kambamba
dialogue.text: Hello! Good morning, my friend. Welcome to our school!

dialogue.speaker: Nzinga
dialogue.text: Good morning! My name is Nzinga. Nice to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: Kambamba
dialogue.text: Nice to meet you too, Nzinga. Where are you from?

content.question: How should Nzinga reply to "Where are you from?"
options: I am fine, thank you very much.
content.explanation: "I am from Luanda, Angola" answers the question "Where are you from?".

activeExercises.title: Classroom Objects & Spelling
activeExercises.instr: Fill in the correct missing letters to name the classroom object.
activeExercises.audioText: Open your notebook and write with your pen.

content.prompt: We write our homework in a note____ and highlight with a yel____ pencil.
content.explanation: Notebook (caderno) and yellow (amarelo) are common classroom vocabulary.

activeExercises.title: Present Simple: Verb To Be
activeExercises.instr: Select the correct form of the verb "to be" (am, is, are).
activeExercises.audioText: Tchissola and Bento are excellent students.

content.question: Tchissola and Bento _____ studying in the school library.
content.explanation: Since "Tchissola and Bento" is plural (They), we use "are".

activeExercises.title: Numbers & Telling the Time
activeExercises.instr: What time is it when the clock shows 07:30 in the morning?
activeExercises.audioText: School starts at half past seven in the morning.

content.question: It is 07:30. In English, we say:
content.explanation: 07:30 is read as "half past seven".

activeExercises.title: Family Members & Possessives
activeExercises.instr: Identify the family relationship in English.

content.question: Your mother's brother is your _____ and his children are your _____.
content.explanation: Mother's brother is an uncle (tio) and his children are cousins (primos).

activeExercises.title: Daily Routines & Adverbs of Frequency
activeExercises.instr: Choose the sentence with correct adverb placement.
activeExercises.audioText: I always wake up early to catch the bus.

content.question: Which sentence has the correct word order?
options: I wake always up at 6 AM.
I always wake up at 6 AM.
Always I wake up 6 AM at.
Wake up I always at 6 AM.
content.explanation: Adverbs of frequency usually go before the main verb: "I always wake up".

activeExercises.title: School Subjects & Preferences
activeExercises.instr: Listen and identify the subject described.
activeExercises.audioText: In this class, we learn about numbers, equations, and geometry.

content.question: Which school subject is described?
content.explanation: Numbers, equations, and geometry are studied in Mathematics.

activeExercises.title: Prepositions of Place
activeExercises.instr: Complete the sentence with the appropriate preposition (in, on, under, between).
activeExercises.audioText: The dictionary is on the teacher desk.

content.question: The dictionary is placed _____ the desk, next to the blackboard.
content.explanation: Objects lying on a surface use the preposition "on".

activeExercises.title: Food, Drinks & Angolan Cuisine
activeExercises.instr: Learn culinary vocabulary and cultural terms in English.
activeExercises.audioText: Muamba de galinha is a famous traditional dish in Angola.

content.question: In English, "peixe grelhado com mandioca" is translated as:
content.explanation: Peixe grelhado = grilled fish; mandioca = cassava.

activeExercises.title: Countable & Uncountable Nouns
activeExercises.instr: Select "many" or "much" according to the noun.
activeExercises.audioText: How much water do you drink every day?

content.question: There isn't _____ milk left, but there are _____ oranges on the table.
content.explanation: "Milk" is uncountable (much); "oranges" are countable plural (many).

activeExercises.title: Past Simple: Regular Verbs
activeExercises.instr: Choose the correct regular past tense form ending in -ed.
activeExercises.audioText: Yesterday, the students visited the National Museum of Anthropology.

content.question: Yesterday, our class _____ (visit) the Kalandula Falls in Malanje.
content.explanation: Regular verbs form the simple past with -ed: "visited".

activeExercises.title: Past Simple: Irregular Verbs
activeExercises.instr: Find the irregular past form for "go" and "see".
activeExercises.audioText: We went to Huambo and saw the beautiful mountain peaks.

content.question: Last weekend we _____ (go) to Benguela and _____ (see) the Atlantic ocean.
content.explanation: The past tense of "go" is "went", and the past of "see" is "saw".

activeExercises.title: Famous Angolan Figures
activeExercises.instr: Read the short biography and answer the question.
activeExercises.audioText: Queen Nzinga Mbandi was a courageous leader in Angolan history.

content.passage: Queen Nzinga Mbandi was a courageous ruler of the Ndongo and Matamba kingdoms in the 17th century. She was famous for her diplomatic skills, strategic brilliance, and defence of her people.
content.question: According to the text, Queen Nzinga was particularly celebrated for her:
content.explanation: The passage highlights her diplomatic skills and defence of her kingdoms.

activeExercises.title: Describing People & Clothes
activeExercises.instr: Select the adjectives that best describe height and personality.
activeExercises.audioText: He is tall, kind, and wears a blue school uniform.

content.question: My best friend has _____ dark hair, is very _____, and always smiles.
content.explanation: "Curly" describes hair texture; "cheerful" (alegre) describes positive temperament.

activeExercises.title: Future Plans: Going to & Will
activeExercises.instr: Express planned intentions versus instant predictions.
activeExercises.audioText: Next year, I am going to study computer science at the academy.

content.question: We have already bought our bus tickets. We _____ travel to Lubango on Friday.
content.explanation: We use "be going to" for intentions that have already been decided and arranged.

activeExercises.title: Angolan Wildlife & Nature
activeExercises.instr: Learn about the giant sable antelope (Palanca Negra Gigante).
activeExercises.audioText: The Giant Sable Antelope is the national symbol of Angola.

content.question: The Giant Sable Antelope (Palanca Negra) is critically protected in which park?
content.explanation: The Giant Sable Antelope is protected in Cangandala National Park, Malanje province.

activeExercises.title: Review Challenge & Quiz
activeExercises.instr: Final comprehensive question for English Grade 8.
activeExercises.audioText: Congratulations on completing all units! Practice makes progress.

content.question: Which question correctly asks for permission in a polite, formal way?
options: May I please borrow your grammar book?
Do you give book to me?
content.explanation: "May I please..." is the standard formal polite expression for requesting permission.
